tiny.examples: 8 GB laptops without a graphics card, phones, older 8 GB Macs

small.examples: 8–12 GB graphics cards, 16 GB Macs and laptops, Steam Deck, ROG Ally

large.examples: 64 GB+ Macs, Ryzen AI Max (Strix Halo), DGX Spark, a 24 GB card with 64 GB+ RAM

selection_rules: From the lab that made it, not a community fine-tune.
A licence anyone can use (Apache 2.0 or MIT) and no access gate.
In the Ollama library and LM Studio, with GGUF and MLX builds from trusted quantisers, so every route on the page works.
Heavily used, and out long enough that the runtimes handle its chat template and tool calls.
Then quality. Novelty alone never earns a slot.

refresh.check: node team/local-ai/fit/tools/check-picks.mjs <models.json>: verifies every pick and file still exists, and lists challengers
refresh.challenger: a model from a listed lab, licence Apache/MIT, ungated, with GGUF + MLX variants from trusted quantisers and an Ollama library tag, whose 30-day downloads (all variants) beat the current pick in the same tier and use, and which is at least 21 days old
refresh.swap: a human (ds-models, or the owner) reads the challenger list and edits PICKS in tools/build-picks.mjs; nothing swaps automatically, because download counts reward novelty and a beginner needs things that work

lmstudio.name: LM Studio
lmstudio.notes: The easiest start: a desktop app with a model browser. Apple Silicon only on Mac (macOS 14+); x64 with AVX2 or Snapdragon on Windows; AppImage on Linux (works on a Steam Deck in Desktop Mode).

ollama.name: Ollama
ollama.notes: One command per model, and a local API other apps can use. Intel GPUs only through Vulkan.

llamacpp.name: llama.cpp
llamacpp.notes: The engine under LM Studio and Ollama, with every option exposed. `llama-server -hf <repo>:<quant>` downloads the model (and its vision projector) and serves a chat page at http://localhost:8080.

mlx.name: MLX
mlx.notes: Apple's own framework, Apple Silicon only. Install with `pip install mlx-lm`; chat with `mlx_lm.chat --model <id>`.
